b1-28-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rules in My Class
b1-28-01.scenario: You are Meg. You are a student in Budapest. Carlos asks what the rules are in your class.
b1-28-01.prompt: Tell Carlos one thing you have to do and one thing that is not allowed.
cues: Say what you have to do
b1-28-01.target: En mi clase hay que llegar a tiempo y no se permite fumar en el edificio.
b1-28-01.english: In my class you have to arrive on time and smoking is not allowed in the building.
b1-28-01.canDo: I can describe rules, obligations and prohibitions.

b1-28-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is Allowed at Work
b1-28-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks what is allowed there.
b1-28-02.prompt: Tell Meg what is allowed and what is not allowed in your office.
b1-28-02.target: En mi oficina está permitido usar el teléfono, pero no se puede fumar.
b1-28-02.english: In my office using the phone is allowed, but you cannot smoke.
b1-28-02.canDo: I can describe what people are allowed to do.

b1-28-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Should Happen
b1-28-03.scenario: You are Meg. You live in Budapest. Carlos asks what you think should happen in public life.
b1-28-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what is necessary and what is important for the government.
cues: Say what is necessary for everyone
Say what is important for the government
b1-28-03.target: Es necesario que todos respeten las reglas y es importante que el gobierno escuche a la gente.
b1-28-03.english: It is necessary that everyone respects the rules and it is important that the government listens to the people.
b1-28-03.canDo: I can discuss what should happen in public life.

b1-28-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why We Follow Rules
b1-28-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks why everyone has to follow a rule at work.
b1-28-04.prompt: Tell Meg why we must follow the rule and what it means for everyone.
cues: Give a reason for the rule
Say what it means for everyone
b1-28-04.target: Debemos cumplir la regla porque protege a todos. Por eso es una responsabilidad de todos.
b1-28-04.english: We must follow the rule because it protects everyone. That is why it is everyone's responsibility.
b1-28-04.canDo: I can discuss rights and responsibilities.

b1-28-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Martí and Our America
b1-28-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a simplified retelling of «Nuestra América», an essay by José Martí, for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what Martí says.
b1-28-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Martí says about the government and about schools.
cues: Say what Martí says about the government
Say what has to be taught in schools
b1-28-05.target: Martí dice que el gobierno tiene que nacer del propio país. También dice que en las escuelas hay que enseñar primero la historia de América.
b1-28-05.english: Martí says that the government has to be born from the country itself. He also says that in schools you have to teach the history of America first.
b1-28-05.canDo: I can defend a position about a difficult rule.

b1-28-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Rule at Work
b1-28-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks what you think about a rule at work.
b1-28-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you think of the rule and why we must respect it.
cues: Say what you think and why
b1-28-consolidation.target: Creo que la regla es necesaria porque protege a todos. Aunque sea incómoda, tenemos la responsabilidad de respetarla.
b1-28-consolidation.english: I think the rule is necessary because it protects everyone. Although it may be inconvenient, we have the responsibility to respect it.
b1-28-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words for rules and obligation.
